module_title: Making of the Constitution & Preamble - Acts, Committees, and Amendments
introduction: At this level, we delve into the specific British Acts that laid the administrative framework, the working mechanisms of the Constituent Assembly (including the Objective Resolution), and the crucial amendments made to the Preamble.

core_concepts.title: Government of India Act, 1935
core_concepts.description: This act was the major source of the Indian Constitution. It provided for a federal setup, the office of the governor, the judiciary, and emergency powers. Over 250 provisions of the Constitution were borrowed from it.

core_concepts.title: The Objective Resolution
core_concepts.description: Moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946, it laid down the fundamentals and philosophy of the constitutional structure. This resolution, once adopted, eventually became the 'Preamble' of the Constitution.

core_concepts.title: 42nd Amendment Act, 1976
core_concepts.description: Known as the 'Mini Constitution', this amendment was enacted during the Emergency. It amended the Preamble for the first and only time, adding three new words: 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity'.

core_concepts.title: Regulating Act (1773) & Pitt's India Act (1784)
core_concepts.description: 1773 designated the Governor of Bengal as the 'Governor-General of Bengal' (Warren Hastings) and created a Supreme Court at Calcutta. 1784 established a system of double government (Board of Control and Court of Directors).

important_entities.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
important_entities.significance: He also chaired the Union Powers Committee and the Union Constitution Committee.

important_entities.name: Sir B.N. Rau
important_entities.significance: He was appointed as the constitutional advisor (Legal Advisor) to the Constituent Assembly and prepared the initial draft of the Constitution.

important_entities.name: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
important_entities.significance: Played a vital role in integrating the princely states and chaired the committee on Fundamental Rights and Minorities.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Is Preamble a part of the Constitution?
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Yes. In the Berubari Union case (1960), the Supreme Court said NO. But in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court reversed its stance and declared that the Preamble IS a part of the Constitution.
Although it is a part of the Constitution, the Preamble is non-justiciable. You cannot go to a court of law to enforce its provisions.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Socialist, Secular, Integrity. These are the ONLY three words ever added to the Preamble.
Any major committee starting with 'Union' was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru. The 'Provincial' committee was chaired by Sardar Patel.

exam_strategy_tips: Match the Following questions frequently pair Major Committees with their Chairmen (e.g., Drafting -> Ambedkar, Union Powers -> Nehru).
Remember that the Preamble has been amended only ONCE so far (1976).
